en.title: Youth protests planned across Europe, organisers expect 160,000 participants
en.dek: Organisers of the Gen Z regelt movement expect over 160,000 participants in Germany's nationwide protests on 31 October, with demonstrations also planned in France and Switzerland.
facts: Organisers expect more than 160,000 participants in Germany.
Protests will take place in Berlin, Cologne, Frankfurt, and Munich, with additional demonstrations planned in France and Switzerland.
The movement demands increased funding for schools, addiction help, psychotherapy, measures against rising living costs, social justice, and climate protection.
Some German retailers closed stores ahead of the protest day, citing concerns about damage or disruption.
body: According to the NZZ, organisers of the Gen Z regelt movement have called for nationwide demonstrations on 31 October, expecting more than 160,000 participants in Germany. The protests will take place in Berlin, Cologne, Frankfurt, and Munich, with additional demonstrations planned in France and Switzerland. The movement demands increased funding for schools, addiction help, psychotherapy, measures against rising living costs, social justice, and climate protection.

The NZZ reports that a German interior minister spokesperson said no evidence of violent calls has been found. However, a spokesperson for the interior ministry noted that some link extremist groups have called to join. The NZZ also reports that German security authorities have no further evidence of violent calls.
The NZZ reports that some German retailers closed stores ahead of the protest day, citing concerns about damage or disruption. Other retailers protected shop windows with boards.

The NZZ reports that in France authorities maintained curfews and restrictions on demonstrations. A court allowed a route between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation to proceed, according to the same source. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the day posed a high risk and announced a large police deployment.

According to the ZDF heute article, the organisers of Gen Z regelt have stated that extremist groups, anti-constitutional symbols, racism, and hate have no place in their movement. They also reject any form of violence.
en.context: The Gen Z regelt movement cites rising housing costs, cuts in education, and social inequality as reasons for the protests. It also demands more climate protection and mental‑health support. The movement is part of a broader trend of youth activism in Europe.
en.imageCaption: Der Staat traktiert die Bürger mit Geld, und doch werden diese immer unzufriedener. Ganz Europa braucht einen neuen Spirit.
